facts.value: SEK 4,000–6,500/month (Uppsala University budget). Fee-paying students are guaranteed a dorm room; EU/EEA/Swiss students must find their own.
SEK 9,500–11,600/month incl. rent (Uppsala University budget; its items sum to up to SEK 12,000).
UL 30-day ticket: SEK 850 at reduced price (students studying ≥75%), adult SEK 1,150; SEK 425 reduced in the 2026 campaign (activate by 2 Dec). UU budget assumes SEK 500.
Mean temperature about −2.0 °C in January and 18.2 °C in July; about 565 mm precipitation/year (SMHI 1991–2020).
facts.notes: Wikipedia climate table citing SMHI 1991–2020 normals; SMHI's own tables were not reached.

facts.value: Classic student city built around the student nations, whose pubs, clubs and restaurants are a hub of student life and offer student jobs.
English is enough for daily life, but many Uppsala employers require Swedish for part-time jobs.
Part-time work in Uppsala is 'very difficult' to find; nation jobs exist but won't cover living costs. Do not rely on work income.
No city data. National example: hotel/restaurant agreement floor SEK 153.64–164.30/hour (from 1 Apr 2026, no experience; youth rates under 20). No statutory minimum wage.
facts.source_name: HRF (Hotel and Restaurant Workers' Union) – Gröna Riksavtalet
facts.notes: A collective-agreement wage floor for one sector, not a measured typical student wage; no citable source for typical student pay found.
